messages:
marie-devex: Heads up — we're going to soft-deprecate the legacy monolithic package `redwood-sdk` next week and publish the new modular packages behind a feature flag. Goal: smaller installs, clearer browser vs server bundles.

alex-sdk: +1. What does the rollout look like? can we do shadow publish then gradual redirect?

sam-platform: Plan I sketched: 1) shadow publish modular packages (npm/pypi) 2) add `X-Use-Modular-SDK` header on a small % of traffic 3) collect telemetry and smoke tests 4) final deprecation announcement 30 days after stable.

marie-devex: exact package names: `@redwood/core`, `@redwood/http`, `@redwood/streams` for npm; `redwood_core`, `redwood_http`, `redwood_streams` for pip. We'll keep `redwood-sdk` as a thin shim that imports core but logs a deprecation warning.

erin-qa: Need migration tests. Can we add a CI matrix job that runs the core tests against the shim and with real examples?

alex-sdk: Yes — I'll add a `migration-smoke` job in the sdk repo that runs the example app against both `redwood-sdk` and the modular combo.

marie-devex: publish window: target Tue 09:00 PT. We'll use deploy-bot to publish canary artifacts first. If deploy-bot reports any checksum or tag mismatch we abort.

deploy-bot: publish job started: #7890 — releasing npm:@redwood/core@1.0.0-canary, pip:redwood_core==1.0.0a0

deploy-bot: npm publish succeeded for @redwood/core@1.0.0-canary (pkg id 7890)

deploy-bot: pip wheel uploaded for redwood_core==1.0.0a0 (pkg id 7890)

nora-eng: Quick question — do we also change the TS/py SDK major version? semver wise this is new packages, but the shim will stay at 0.x for backward compat.

alex-sdk: We'll keep the shim at the current major and bump the modular packages to 1.0.0. Add deprecation message in `__init__.py`/index.ts: `DeprecationWarning: redwood-sdk is deprecated; please migrate to @redwood/core` with link to migration guide.

marie-devex: Rollback criteria: 1) >1% error increase on golden routes; 2) packaging checksum mismatch; 3) pip/npm repudiation errors. If any hit, we yank canary and stop the header rollout.

erin-qa: Add a regression eval in Redwood Console: compare tokenization and generation sample outputs for the same prompts to avoid silent behavior changes.

sam-platform: also add telemetry tag `sdk_modular_canary=true` so product queries are filterable.

alex-sdk: For publishing sequence I'll do: canary npm/pip -> smoke tests -> promote npm tag `canary`->`latest` and pypi release. Promote only after 2 hours stable and green migration-smoke CI.

marie-devex: Docs: I'll draft the deprecation notice + migration guide. We should include quick install snippets and example code. Erin, can you proof the examples?

erin-qa: Yep. I'll run the examples against the internal examples repo and confirm compat.

marie-devex: One more ops thing: add a short-lived pin in the release-notes repo so older projects can pin `redwood-sdk==<current>` if they need more time.

nora-eng: Sounds good. Also add a small note in CHANGELOG about memory improvements and reduced browser bundle by ~60% for the modular split.

deploy-bot: publish job completed: all canary artifacts published. CI trigger: migration-smoke started (run id 562).

marie-devex: Awesome — I’ll post the soft-deprecation announcement to the SDK docs and draft the support KB. We'll wait for migration-smoke results before promoting. :thumbsup:

alex-sdk: If anything looks off we can delay promote and keep shim warnings for 60 days.

marie-devex: Agreed. Thanks everyone.
